keyVerseText: And it shall be at that day, saith the LORD, that thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali. Ishi: that is, My husband Baali: that is, My lord
rootMeaning: The root of בַּעֲלִי (Baʻălîy) is בַּעַל (baʻal), a Hebrew term rich with meanings including lord, master, husband, and chief. The suffix in בַּעֲלִי indicates possession, translating the word as "my lord" or "my master." This literal sense conveys a personal and authoritative relationship, emphasizing possession and intimate lordship beyond a mere title.
usageInScripture: The word בַּעֲלִי appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Hosea 2:16, where it is translated as "Baali" meaning "my lord." This singular occurrence highlights its use as a symbolic name for Jehovah, contrasting with its association as a deity in the northern kingdom. The consistent translation as "my lord" underscores its role in expressing a relational and covenantal lordship rather than a generic title.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בַּעֲלִי as "my lord" rooted in the concept of ownership and authority deepens our grasp of God's personal relationship with His people. It reflects the intimate bond between God and His covenant community, where God is not only sovereign but personally committed as husband and master. This term challenges believers to recognize the exclusivity and devotion owed to God alone, distinguishing Him from false deities. The use of בַּעֲלִי as a symbolic name for Jehovah also reveals the tension in Israel's history between true worship and idolatry, pointing to the necessity of faithfulness to the one true Lord.
keyVerseReflection: In Hosea 2:16, God declares, "thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali," where Baali means "my lord." This verse marks a shift from a term that could be associated with false gods to one emphasizing a personal and faithful relationship, "Ishi" meaning "my husband." The word בַּעֲלִי here highlights the transformation from a possibly distant or contested lordship to an intimate, covenantal bond, inviting believers to a deeper understanding of God's faithful love and lordship.
